1. The shape of a molecule is determined by repulsions between all of the electron pairs present in the valence shell.
2. Valence shell electron pairs repel one another since their electron clouds are negatively charged.
3. These pairs tend to occupy positions in space that minimize repulsion and maximize distance between them.
4. The magnitude of repulsion follows the order: $\text{Lone pair-Lone pair (lp-lp)} > \text{Lone pair-Bond pair (lp-bp)} > \text{Bond pair-Bond pair (bp-bp)}$.
proTip: Keep the order of repulsive forces (lp-lp > lp-bp > bp-bp) handy as it explains bond angle distortions.
